title: K Closest Points to Origin
prompt:
Given an array of `points` where `points[i] = [xi, yi]` represents a point on the X-Y plane and an integer `k`, return the `k` closest points to the origin `(0, 0)`.

The distance between two points on the X-Y plane is the Euclidean distance (i.e. `sqrt((x1 - x2)^2 + (y1 - y2)^2)`). You may return the answer in any order; the answer is guaranteed to be unique (except for the order in which it is returned).

examples.explanation: Distance of (1,3) from origin is sqrt(10). Distance of (-2,2) from origin is sqrt(8). Since sqrt(8) < sqrt(10), (-2,2) is closer, so it is the answer.
The distances are sqrt(18), sqrt(26), sqrt(20). The two closest are (3,3) and (-2,4), returned here in the order this solution's heap produces them (any order is accepted).

hints: Sorting all points by distance takes O(n log n) — can you avoid a full sort when you only need the closest k?
A max-heap of size k lets you track the k closest points seen so far: if a new point is closer than the current farthest of the k, swap it in.
Compare squared distances instead of taking square roots — it avoids floating point and comparisons are equivalent since distance is non-negative.

solution.approach: Maintain a max-heap (via negated squared distance) of at most k points. For each point, compute its squared distance from the origin (no need for sqrt since it's monotonic and only used for comparison), push it onto the heap, and pop the farthest point if the heap exceeds size k. After processing all points, the heap contains exactly the k closest ones. This is O(n log k) instead of O(n log n) for a full sort.
